The commercial pilot one ($152k) is absolutely wrong. Most pilots are lucky to even get above 70K. They start at around 25K annually, and then slowly start to accrue experience to climb the ladder, getting small salary increases. If something happens to their airline or they have to leave, they start at the BOTTOM of the new airline's seniority system, and they have to start all over again. If any pilots manage to get a 6 figure salary, it's the grey haired 50 year old captains who were never furloughed or fired. The ones nearing the end of their career after having a successful career at a major airline their whole life. Not to mention the cost of flight training for those who do not want to serve in the air force. This can end up at nearly $120K. There is a reason for flight training to cost so much, but that doesn't excuse it from the fact that 120K is a lot of money. If anyone managed to take out a loan of that much, they would end up paying in excess of 150K back to the lender, owing to interest rates. If they end up working for an airline as a commercial pilot, they need to find a way to ensure they can live somewhere and have all the bare necessities, leaving virtually nothing in the kitty for paying back that very hefty loan.
